subject: MAP: Pilot acceptance, exit gates & test owners — Medvera pilot
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@medvera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — proposed acceptance tests, exit gates, owners (draft)

Hi Sarah — great to meet yesterday and thanks for the time. Per our conversation I put together a focused mutual action plan for the 6-week pilot that spells out: success criteria, exit gates, concrete acceptance tests, and primary owners.

High-level ask: can you review the acceptance tests below and confirm owners on your side by EOD next Wednesday (8/20)? Once agreed we’ll lock the MAP worksheet and align delivery milestones in the SOW.

Summary of proposed success criteria (pass = green / fail = red):
- Latency: median inference latency <= 220ms for 90% of production-like requests (50–512 tokens)
- Accuracy: task-level F1 >= 0.86 on the blinded evaluation set (folder: eval_acceptance_tests.md)
- Throughput: sustained throughput >= 150 concurrent sessions without degradation beyond 10% of baseline
- Safety: false-positive rate on the profanity/blocklist test < 0.5%
- Operational: end-to-end deploy, rollback, and traceability exercised at least once during pilot

Exit gates (stop / proceed):
- Stop: any single safety test failure with high-risk content that cannot be mitigated within 48 hours
- Stop: repeated SLA breach (3 incidents in a rolling 7-day window)
- Proceed to expansion: all green on the acceptance test matrix and SOC2 audit items marked as "evidence provided"

Ownership & acceptance tests (example rows):
- Data ingest sampling (owner: Medvera data ops) — verify sample coverage >= 95% of planned clinics
- Eval harness run (owner: Redwood QA / Karthik) — run blinded eval, record F1/precision/recall
- Latency benchmarking (owner: Redwood infra / Marissa) — continuous run under synthetic load with KV caching config v1
- Safety probe suite (owner: Medvera trust & safety + Redwood research) — 3 curated prompt families, pass threshold per family

Attachments: MEDV_MAP_v0.3.xlsx (MAP timeline + RACI), eval_acceptance_tests.md (test definitions), SOC2_evidence_overview.pdf (inventory).

Next steps suggested:
1) You confirm owners for the 4 Medvera-side items listed above (data ingest, evaluation steward, trust lead, procurement point)
2) We schedule a 30-min alignment on Friday 8/15 to walk the acceptance tests and talk rollback triggers
3) Redwood to create a cutover checklist and a canary rollout plan referencing the MAP cells 3–7 in the workbook

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri…@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0191

---
Attachment stubs:
- Medvera_MAP_v0.3.xlsx (workbook, 3 sheets)
- eval_acceptance_tests.md (markdown, 1.8KB)
- SOC2_evidence_overview.pdf (stub, 120KB)

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@medvera.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medvera.com
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — proposed acceptance tests, exit gates, owners (draft)

Thanks, Priyom — this is a helpful starting point. Quick clarifying notes before our Friday call: 

1) Latency: the 220ms median target looks reasonable but can you confirm tail percentiles (p95/p99) under expected hospital Wi‑Fi conditions? We need concrete numbers to evaluate UX risk.
2) Accuracy: the eval set — is that the v2 blinded set we discussed? Who will hold the gold labels?
3) Safety: we will need an agreed remediation window for low/medium severity safety flags; 48 hours sounds tight for some legal review items. Can we propose severity buckets and SLAs per bucket?
4) SOC2: procurement needs a short inventory of what evidence Redwood will provide during the pilot (not full audit, just sample artifacts).

Owners at Medvera (tentative):
- Data ingest: Marco Alvarez (dataops@medvera.com)
- Trust & safety: Sarah Chen (me)
- Procurement lead: procurement@medvera.com

I’m available for the 8/15 11:00am slot if that works. Also, can you add a failure-mode scenario section to the MAP (e.g., noisy data causing drift, KV cache misconfiguration causing latency spikes) with mitigation owners? That’ll help our risk committee.

–Sarah
Sarah Chen
Director, Applied AI — Medvera Health
sarah.chen@medvera.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@medvera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — proposed acceptance tests, exit gates, owners (draft)

Sarah — thanks, great questions. Short answers and updates below; I’ve also added a failure-mode table to the workbook (sheet: failure_modes).

- Tail latency: proposed p95 <= 480ms, p99 <= 850ms under a 95th-percentile hospital Wi‑Fi profile (we ran the same profile in our lab). We’ll include the raw traces and bandwidth assumptions in the MAP attachment.
- Eval set: yes, this is the v2 blinded set. Redwood will host the eval runner; Medvera retains gold labels. Results are submitted to a read-only S3 bucket for cross-checking.
- Safety SLA: agree on buckets. Proposed: Critical (legal/privacy) — 24h response; High — 48h; Medium — 5 business days. We’ll call out owners in the MAP.
- SOC2 evidence: see SOC2_evidence_overview.pdf in attachments — it lists sample logs, RBAC screenshots, and a short retention summary we can drop into a procurement pack.

I attached MAP_v0.3 with a Failure Modes table and explicit mitigation owners. Key mitigation examples:
- Noisy data -> quarantine pipeline + rerun with sampling (owner: Marco at Medvera; Redwood assists)
- KV cache misconfig -> revert to config v0.9 and disable cross-session caching (owner: Redwood infra — Marissa)
- Performance regression after quantization -> fallback to FP16 variant and trigger root-cause perf trace (owner: Karthik / Redwood research)

Proposal for timeline (high-level):
- Week 0 (agreement): owners confirmed, MAP locked, SOW amendment signed
- Week 1: environment prep, sample ingest, baseline latency runs
- Week 2–3: blinded eval runs + safety probe suite
- Week 4: canary cutover (10% traffic) + smoke acceptance tests
- Week 5: ramp to 50% with continuous monitoring
- Week 6: final acceptance run and decision call

Canary/rollback rules will be explicit in the MAP: any critical safety flag during canary -> immediate rollback; p99 > 1s for >10m -> rollback.

I’m good for 8/15 11:00am — inviting you and Marco.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@medvera.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — proposed acceptance tests, exit gates, owners (draft)

Looping in a couple of operational points from Redwood infra/ops perspective:

1) Acceptance test ownership must include specific runbooks and owners who can execute within SLA windows. Karthik — can you confirm the QA runbook owner and who will run the blinded eval? Recommend: Karthik (lead) + 1 engineer backup.
2) Evidence capture: every acceptance test must produce an artifact (timestamped log, trace, or exported metrics) that we attach to the MAP evidence folder. This avoids manual reconciliation at signoff.
3) Canary checklist: we need a pre-canary checklist with 8 items (health checks, circuit breakers, throttles, alert hooks). I put a checklist template in the workbook.

Specific edits I made in MAP_v0.3: added a column "acceptance_artifact" and a required artifact type per test; added a "run_owner_backup" field.

From an internal SLA posture, if Medvera requires a different retention or audit cadence we should note that in the SOW and mark those MAP rows as contract-bound (not pilot-only). Procurement — please flag any artifacts that must be preserved beyond the pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Cloud Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@medvera.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Alvarez <dataops@medvera.com>, procurement@medvera.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2025 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — proposed acceptance tests, exit gates, owners (draft)

Thanks — this reads well and the failure-mode table addresses our main concerns. A few final items from procurement & trust that we need before we lock: 

- Procurement asks for the SOC2 evidence summary in an editable spreadsheet rather than PDF. Can Redwood provide a CSV of the evidence inventory? (procurement@medvera.com)
- Trust asks for the remediation SLA table to be added to the MAP front page (we’ll sign off once that is visible).
- Medvera confirms owners: Marco (data ingest), Sarah (trust), procurement@medvera.com (procurement).

If those three small asks are done by Tue 9/2 we can keep the 6-week calendar intact and start Week 0 on Mon 9/8. If anything slips we’ll have to push the canary into late Sep.

I’ll plan to review the CSV once you send it. Appreciate the fast turnaround on the failure modes.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Applied AI — Medvera Health
